headline: Bangladesh on cusp of historic Test victory against world No. 1 Australia in Darwin
summary: Bangladesh has dominated Australia in the ongoing Test in Darwin, taking a significant lead and putting the world's top-ranked Test side under immense pressure. This potential upset echoes past instances where Bangladesh's victories led to major overhauls in g
details: Bangladesh's pace attack, spearheaded by Hasan Mahmud's six-wicket haul, dismissed world No. 1 Australia for just 198 in their first innings. Bangladesh then responded with a commanding 426, featuring Tanzid Hasan's maiden century and Najmul Hossain Shanto's 84.

This gave Bangladesh a significant 228-run lead. At stumps on day three, Australia were 161 for 4 in their second innings, still trailing by 67 runs, with Cameron Green and Alex Carey steadying the innings after an early collapse.

This potential victory, thousands of kilometres from Australia's traditional cricketing heartland in Darwin, marks a rare occasion. Bangladesh is taking apart the world's top Test side at an unusual venue in a rare winter Test window.

Historically, Bangladesh has been a catalyst for change in world cricket. In the 2007 50-over World Cup, their upset victory over India led to India's team overhaul, the rise of T20 cricket, and an ICC tournament format change.

Similarly, Bangladesh's elimination of England in the 2015 World Cup prompted England's reinvention of their ODI approach. This aggressive strategy ultimately led England to lift the World Cup trophy four years later.

A comprehensive win by a visiting Asian side on Australian soil is a rare feat, with only India and Pakistan achieving Test victories there in recent decades. Sri Lanka has never won a Test match in Australia.

Such an upset, with the No. 9 ranked side beating the No. 1, would inject crucial relevance into the World Test Championship. It would also highlight Bangladesh's recurring role in forcing cricket's superpowers to reassess their strategies.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[apologises for power and gas crisis]], promises improvement soon
headline: PM Tarique Rahman apologises for power and gas crisis, promises improvement soon
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has issued a sincere apology to the nation for the ongoing power and gas shortages, assuring that urgent measures are underway to significantly improve the situation within days.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman yesterday apologised to the people for the ongoing power and gas shortages, assuring urgent steps to ease the crisis. He expressed hope that the situation would improve significantly within the next few days.

Speaking at a cheque distribution and doa mahfil programme, the PM urged political parties criticising the government to propose concrete, workable plans instead of creating confusion. The event also marked the 80th birth anniversary of late prime minister Khaleda Zia.

Tarique attributed the current gas shortage to Bangladesh’s limited LNG storage and regasification capacity. He noted that over the past 17 years, previous governments did not explore new gas fields, making the sector dependent on foreign sources.

He explained that the country's import facilities are limited to two vessels, and an accident involving one of them exacerbated the crisis. The previous government's initiative for a third vessel was cancelled by an interim government.

The Prime Minister stated that technical problems have already been addressed and his government is working to free people from this hardship. They are collaborating with China and other countries to expedite the construction and deployment of a new vessel.

He also spoke with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim seeking assistance with gas requirements. Tarique urged patience, highlighting that specialized LNG vessels take considerable time to build and are produced by only a limited number of countries.

Challenging critics, the PM invited any party with a realistic plan to solve the problems within six months to present it to parliament and the people, promising implementation. He stressed that people desire development and accountability, not street agitation.
